summary: Converted the durable workflow schema and deterministic seed to vendor-neutral Railway PostgreSQL migrations, removed retired platform scheduling artifacts, and verified advisory-lock, bounded-claim, durable-lease, and outcome-unknown recovery behavior on PostgreSQL 17.

commands: PostgreSQL 17 scratch cluster: apply database/migrations/*.sql in timestamp order and run psql -f tests/database/launch_workflow.sql
tests.notes: Six migration-path and portability tests passed. A fresh PostgreSQL 17 cluster applied both migrations and passed the transactional database suite covering deterministic inert reset, immutable and consecutively versioned events, idempotency uniqueness, provider allowlists, transaction-scoped scheduler lock acquisition, bounded SKIP LOCKED claims, one active lease per resource, stale-claim recovery, outcome_unknown conversion, and reconciliation-before-retry. The optional pglast parser was unavailable, but PostgreSQL itself parsed and executed all migration and test SQL.

notes_for_next_agent: Apply database/migrations/*.sql in timestamp order through the Railway release/pre-deploy migration runner using only the API service's private DATABASE_URL; these migrations contain no environment URL or credential.

The in-process API poller should call try_scheduler_lock(scenario_id) inside its claim transaction, then use claim_scheduled_actions and claim_outbox with bounded limits. PostgreSQL due times, claims, and leases remain scheduler authority.

recover_stale_claims makes unattempted expired work retryable but converts any possibly accepted provider send to outcome_unknown and marks its provider attempt reconciliation_required. Do not retry that action until provider identity, signed callback, or manual recovery establishes the outcome.

The fixed finals scenario UUID remains 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111. reset_finals_scenario() restores fixed seed state and the inert T-3/T-1 schedule without leaving outbox, provider-attempt, or webhook effects.

The Railway connection role owns runtime least-privilege configuration. Platform-specific client roles, extension-based schedulers, secret stores, and database-owned HTTP scheduling are not part of this target.
